items.text: NDA (after 12th) and TES (10+2, JEE-based) are the earliest officer-entry doors; CDS is the main route after a bachelor's degree.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: A pay table or a pension rule cannot tell you whether a defence career actually fits your temperament and your family's situation.

A defence career rewards people who can sit with discipline, hierarchy, and physical demand for years without treating it as a temporary phase, and who genuinely want to lead or serve alongside people under real pressure, not just wear the uniform in family photos.

If the idea of daily physical training, drill, and strict hierarchy for years genuinely drains you rather than steadies you, that is a real signal worth taking seriously before you commit a training slot.
A defence services career India delivers real stability, respect, and structure, but it also asks for things most desk-job career comparisons never mention.
Officers and other ranks get posted where the service needs them, field areas, high-altitude posts, remote border locations, and peace stations in rotation, typically every 2-3 years.

Medical standards for defence entries are strict and specific (eyesight, BMI, dental, and more), and a disqualification at the SSB medical stage after months of preparation is a genuinely common outcome.

blocks.heading: Waste an Attempt or Years of Service

items.text: NDA and TES training itself weeds out people who cannot sustain years of drill, physical training, and hierarchy, test your own tolerance honestly before you commit at 17.
Only Permanent Commission officers, and SSC officers who cross the relevant service threshold or are later granted PC, draw a service pension.
Decide, with your family, whether you can genuinely sustain transfers every 2-3 years, extended separations, and remote postings before you sign up, not after your first posting order arrives.

blocks.heading: Defence Services Career, in One Table
rows: NDA (National Defence Academy)
Class 12 pass, unmarried, 16.5-19.5 years. Army wing accepts any stream; Navy and Air Force wings require Physics and Mathematics.
UPSC written exam (Maths + General Ability) twice a year, then SSB interview and medical.
CDS (Combined Defence Services)
Bachelor's degree in any discipline. Age band differs by academy: roughly 19-24 for IMA, 19-22 for INA, 19-23 for AFA, and 19-25 for OTA (non-technical, no pension track).
Technical Entry Scheme (TES)
Selection uses your JEE Main score directly.

No separate written exam from the Army. Shortlisting on JEE Main score, then SSB and medical. Selected candidates get a fully funded 4-year B.Tech at an Army engineering college, commissioned as Lieutenant on completion.
Agnipath (Agniveer, other ranks)
10th or 12th pass depending on trade, 17.5-21 years for Navy and 17.5-23 years for Army and Air Force. Open to men and women depending on service and trade.
Written/online test, physical fitness test, medical, and merit list.

blocks.heading: Under the 7th CPC Defence Pay Matrix
rows: Basic pay band (7th CPC)

The defence pay matrix runs from Level 3 to Level 18, with a minimum basic pay around Rs 21,700 (other ranks entry) and a maximum near Rs 2,50,000 (service chief level). Officers commissioned via NDA/CDS/TES start around Level 10.
Military Service Pay (MSP)

A fixed monthly addition on top of basic pay: Rs 15,500 for commissioned officers (Level 10 and above) and Rs 5,200 for JCOs and other ranks (Level 1-9). MSP counts toward DA, HRA, and other percentage-linked allowances.
Allowances

Beyond basic pay and MSP, officers and other ranks draw Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance (where applicable), and a range of service-specific allowances, field area, high-altitude, siachen, flying, submarine, and hardship allowances among others, depending on posting and role.
Non-cash perks

Free rations or ration money, subsidised officers' mess or barrack accommodation, Canteen Stores Department (CSD) access for duty-free goods, and free or heavily subsidised medical care for self and family while in service.
Group insurance and welfare funds
Army/Navy/Air Force Group Insurance schemes provide low-cost life cover during service, along with service-specific welfare and benevolent funds for the officer and family.

blocks.heading: Ladder and How Fast It Actually Moves

items.text: A commissioned officer starts as a Lieutenant (Sub-Lieutenant in the Navy, Flying Officer in the Air Force) and moves to Captain (Lieutenant in Navy, Flight Lieutenant in Air Force) around 2 years of service, then to Major (Lieutenant Commander, Squadron Leader) around the 6-year mark, largely on time-scale promotion rather than a competitive board.

Officers with roughly 13 years of commissioned service move to the Lieutenant Colonel rank (Commander in Navy, Wing Commander in Air Force), which sits at Pay Level 12A in the 7th CPC defence pay matrix.

Colonel rank (roughly 16 years of service, Pay Level 13) and Brigadier rank (Pay Level 13A) are selection-based, not time-based, and a meaningful share of officers who reach Lieutenant Colonel do not go further, simply because there are far fewer Colonel and Brigadier posts than Lieutenant Colonels competing for them.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Permanent Commission officers and other ranks who complete the pensionable qualifying period (broadly 20 years for officers, shorter for some other-ranks categories) draw a pension based on rank and last pay drawn. Short Service Commission officers who leave before 10-14 years and are not granted Permanent Commission generally do not get a service pension, this is the single biggest financial difference between the two tracks.
